Tori Trades · top-down trendlines

This notebook draws the trendlines that Tori Trades teaches in her video Once you master this strategy, trading becomes EASY (2026-09-24) automatically, for any stock in the database. It only draws the lines: no entries, no exits, no backtest (her trade rules are parked in IDEAS.md). What she does by hand, and the exact rule used here (topdown.py):
  1. Rays. She draws every line with TradingView's ray tool: point A, point B, extended to the right; downward lines connect swing highs, upward lines swing lows. A line is a ray from point A to the right edge; downward lines rest on the candles' highs, upward lines under their lows.
  2. Start at the extreme. She starts on the monthly chart with all history in view: the first downward line starts at the highest point on the chart, the first upward line at the lowest. The same, over every daily candle the database holds (section 1).
  3. Price never cuts through a line. She turns the ray as far as it goes and catches as many touches as possible. The steepest ray from point A that touches a candle and that no later candle goes through; a poke too small to see does not count (the "too small to see" slider). Of all the rays from A that no candle crosses, this one also passes closest to every candle, so it has the most touches.
  4. Close enough is a touch. A candle whose high (low) comes within "close enough" typical candles of the line touches it; a typical candle is the median high-to-low range of the candles on the chart. A touch counts once "confirm" candles have followed it.
  5. Lines connect. Each new line starts at the previous line's point B, its most recent touch, and is steeper. Point B is the most recent touch, and the next line starts there. Every later candle stays further from the line than B, so the next line is always steeper. A ray stopped by a candle that is still too new is not a line yet: it is drawn dashed (pending).
  6. Top-down. Then the weekly, daily, 4-hour and 1-hour charts, and finally the trading chart (15 minutes in her example, anything from 5 minutes to 1 hour); on each lower chart she tidies the lines and adds the steeper ones it shows. Every chart after the monthly shows its last "screen" candles. The walk restarts at the last point A or B left of the screen, moved onto the candle of this chart that holds its price: that redraws the lines reaching onto the screen with the precise candles and adds the steeper lines only this chart can see. Lines that end left of the screen keep their drawing from the higher chart, unless a candle on this screen goes through one: then it is drawn again too.
Time runs on one trading-session clock on every chart. Session n starts at n, and a 15-minute candle opening at 10:00 sits at n + 30/390. Nights, weekends and holidays take no room (as on a TradingView chart), so a line has one slope on every chart. A monthly or weekly candle sits at its first session, as a chart places a candle at its opening time. The day of its high only shows on a lower chart: that is why the lower charts adjust the lines.

data.text/html:
1 · The candles

NOW: daily candles from 2015-01-02 to 2026-10-16 (2965 sessions); 1-minute candles of the regular session: 2024-12-26 to 2026-10-16. The walk sees everything up to the close of 2026-10-16. Monthly and weekly candles are built from the daily ones; the 4-hour, 1-hour, 15- and 5-minute candles from the 1-minute ones, regular session only, each counted from the 09:30 open (a 4-hour chart has a 09:30 and a 13:30 candle, as on TradingView). Before the first 1-minute session, the intraday charts lean on the daily candles. Tori starts from the very first candle a stock ever traded. Here, all history means the database's daily history: if NOW traded before 2015-01-02, those highs and lows are missing, and a side's first line can start elsewhere than on her chart (ServiceNow, for one, listed in June 2012).

2 · The top-down walk, chart by chart

Each tab is one chart of the walk, with the lines as they stand after it. Red lines run along the highs (downward lines), blue lines under the lows (upward lines). A line is the thicker, the higher the chart it was drawn on. Diamonds are points A and B (B is a line's latest touch and the next line's A); open circles are candles that touch a line. A dashed ray is pending: the candle that stops it is among the last confirm candles, so it is no touch yet. Hover over a line for its points and slope.
The monthly chart, all 142 candles (all history). downward: 0 line(s) drawn or adjusted on this chart; the next ray, from 2025-01-02, is stopped by the candle of 2026-10-01, still too new to count (dashed). Its first point A is the highest high of all history: 2025-01-02 at 239.62 · upward: 2 line(s) drawn or adjusted on this chart; the next ray, from 2026-07-01, is stopped by the candle of 2026-10-01, still too new to count (dashed). Its first point A is the lowest low of all history: 2016-02-01 at 9.20.
The weekly chart, its last 150 candles, from 2023-12-04. downward: 0 line(s) drawn or adjusted on this chart; the next ray, from 2025-01-27, is stopped by the candle of 2026-10-12, still too new to count (dashed) · upward: 3 line(s) drawn or adjusted on this chart; the next ray, from 2026-09-28, is stopped by the candle of 2026-10-12, still too new to count (dashed).
The daily chart, its last 150 candles, from 2026-03-16. downward: 0 line(s) drawn or adjusted on this chart; the next ray, from 2025-01-28, is stopped by the candle of 2026-10-16, still too new to count (dashed) · upward: 4 line(s) drawn or adjusted on this chart; the next ray, from 2026-09-30, is stopped by the candle of 2026-10-15, still too new to count (dashed).
The 4-hour chart, its last 150 candles, from 2026-07-02 09:30. downward: 0 line(s) drawn or adjusted on this chart; the next ray, from 2025-01-28 09:30, is stopped by the candle of 2026-10-16 09:30, still too new to count (dashed) · upward: 2 line(s) drawn or adjusted on this chart, 2 kept from the charts above; the next ray, from 2026-09-30 09:30, is stopped by the candle of 2026-10-16 09:30, still too new to count (dashed).
The 1-hour chart, its last 150 candles, from 2026-09-17 13:30. downward: 1 line(s) drawn or adjusted on this chart; the next ray, from 2026-10-16 09:30, is stopped by the candle of 2026-10-16 15:30, still too new to count (dashed) · upward: 2 line(s) drawn or adjusted on this chart, 3 kept from the charts above; the next ray, from 2026-10-16 13:30, is stopped by the candle of 2026-10-16 14:30, still too new to count (dashed).
The 15-minute chart, its last 150 candles, from 2026-10-09 11:00. downward: 1 line(s) drawn or adjusted on this chart; the next ray, from 2026-10-16 09:30, is stopped by the candle of 2026-10-16 15:45, still too new to count (dashed) · upward: 1 line(s) drawn or adjusted on this chart, 4 kept from the charts above; the next ray, from 2026-10-16 15:00, is stopped by the candle of 2026-10-16 15:45, still too new to count (dashed).

3 · The result on the 15-minute chart

Every line of the walk on the trading chart, as of the close of 2026-10-16. Light candles came later; the lines never saw them. Move the as-of date back to replay a stretch, as Tori does with TradingView's replay.

4 · How one line is found

Pick a line of the result. The figure shows the line's chart from point A on: the rays from A that are steeper than the line (each goes through the candle that stopped it), the band within which a candle touches, the touches, and point B, where the next line starts. The three sliders are the same as at the top.

From point A (2025-01-28 11:00, 239.62) the ray turns down as far as it can, until the candle of 2026-10-16 09:30 (star) stops it: every steeper ray (dotted) runs through that candle. The line changes -0.198 per session. A candle whose high comes within 0.16 of it (the grey band, close enough on the 15-minute chart) touches it: 3 15-minute candles (open circles). The latest touch followed by at least 2 candles is point B (2026-10-16 09:30, 154.20). No later candle can stop a ray from B yet, so the chain ends here. The line was drawn on the 15-minute chart; its life is too long to show in those candles, so they are the daily ones.

5 · The lines, and the rule checks

Every confirmed line on the 15-minute chart: its points, the candle that stopped the ray, its slope, where it stands at the last candle and how far the last close (141.93) is from it.Her rules, checked on every chart of the walk: no candle on a chart's screen goes through a line (beyond too small to see), every line is steeper than the one before, and every line starts at the previous line's point B. The first column should read 0 and the other two True.
